name: 1816 Prairie Avenue — Charles M. Henderson house

grade.why: Pictured: 2 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), and the photograph (after 1873) shows the same plan. Its building and loss dates are not read here.

placement.position_note: The main body's rear south corner: lot frame u 34.30, v -4.72 m (the draft's frame point u 11.55, v -4.97 through its own rotation), where the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1816-b1) puts the front block's south wall and the rear range's end. The draft's fit of the sheet stands behind it (its georeference's independent check 1.47 m RMS). Rotation -0.621 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1816 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1816 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The front block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1816-b1 p2) in the lot's frame: its south wall at v -4.72, its north wall at v 10.10, the front at u 46.0-46.6 (taken at 46.3) and the rear range's end at u 34.3. The canted bays, the porch and the rear range stand on it as K08 bays, the door's porch and a K01 rear wing.

stories.note: Two storeys of brick over a raised stone basement, under a mansard: the photograph's walls stop at a bracketed cornice over the second storey and the roof's lower faces rise over it with dormers in them. The 1911 sheet's '3S.B.' counts the mansard's attic as its third storey, as it does at 1620 and 1736.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet: '3S.B.; rear2B brick dwelling (D)'; the photograph shows what its brick stands on: a basement of smooth light ashlar from grade to a projecting water table at the principal floor, run round the street front, both canted bays and the south flank, with the brick only over it. T-1886: built as K01's stone front stopped at the principal floor (stone_front.brick_above_m), as 1834's and 1708's are; the sheet's 'brick' is the walls over it.

principal_floor_m.note: The principal floor at the top of the rusticated stone basement, the stone basement's top band at y 885 px at the south-east corner, about 2.0 m over grade at the camera's 53.6 px/m there, through the photograph's camera (data/reference_views/henderson_house_1816_prairie/chicagology_photo.json); the porch's floor and the stoop's landing stand on it.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, principal storey first, read through the photograph's camera at the street front's south corner (53.6 px/m, the corner 46 m from the eye): the upper sills at y 590 px, 5.5 m over the principal floor, and the brackets' foot at y 355 px, 11.9 m over grade: the second storey's sills and the cornice's soffit put the wall head about 12.1 m over grade.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K03 common brick panel 1620 wears; the print is monochrome.

face_brick.note: T-3385: Chicagology's photograph reads the front's brick at 0.65-0.70 of its slate's reflectance (a red; a buff reads 1.5) and well under its white trim; the side wall paler. Pressed red front, common buff sides. Palette: data/components/prairie_1904/k03_face_brick.json; the reading: docs/RESEARCH/face-brick-1904-T-3385/README.md (L-k03-face-brick-3385). The north flank, the rear and the rear range keep the common: no picture shows them (L-k01-1816-henderson-1886).

street_front_trim.note: Every street window under a stone hood on both storeys, as the photograph draws them: K09's cornice-hood lintel. T-1886: the south flank's window (side_bays 6.4) wears the same hood on both storeys (`lights`), where the brick wall had arched it in brick: the photograph draws it with the front's hood, its consoles and its crest (x 350-385 px); and every such hood carries a carved crest (`crest`, K09's T-3270 palmette between two volutes), the print's raised scrolled cresting over each hood, about 1.0 m wide and 0.35 m high through the solved camera. The crest's carving is the kit's (the print resolves only a raised scrolled block); the canted bays' K08 windows keep the bays' own lintels, crested with the same carving (bays[].storeys[].windows[].crest).

wall_head.note: A bracketed cornice round the walls under the mansard: the photograph shows its brackets in pairs under a deep corona along the front and the south flank. K10's bracketed timber cornice; its bracket rhythm is the kit's.

roof_form.note: A mansard: the photograph's roof rises in steep slated lower faces over the cornice, with dormers in them, to a deck railed with iron cresting.

roof_pitch_deg.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the mansard's upper deck at 10 degrees, as 1620's; the photograph shows only its cresting.

side_bays.note: One window a storey on the south flank between its canted bay and the front corner, next to the bay, as the photograph shows; the flank toward the front corner is blank in it.

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: one window a storey on the main body's rear wall south of the rear range; no picture sees the rear.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K06 two-over-two flat sash and area lights 1620 wears; the photograph shows two-over-two sash in the principal windows. T-1886: the light over the door, opening onto the porch's balcony, is K06's French window (two casement leaves to the floor under a transom), the kit's own reconstruction of a balcony door (1637's, T-2534); its foot is behind the balcony's guard in the photograph, which shows its head and upper glass only.

entrance_kit.note: The photograph's porch: the door behind a flight straight down to the walk, two turned columns on plinths at the landing's front corners and a respond against the wall behind each, an entablature over them about 0.6 m deep under a moulded cornice, and on it an iron balcony railing. Built on the K01 door hood (T-2480) widened to the 1911 sheet's 3.1 m porch and standing 2.0 m out on columns (T-2963, `hood.columns`); its soffit 5.9 m over grade is read through the camera. The capitals are carved in the print (open on the match record) and the railing's pierced iron panels are the kit's square balusters in iron. The sheet colours the porch frame, so the columns and entablature are painted timber. T-1886 (2026-11-13): the balcony's guard raised to 0.95 m, about a metre as the print's pierced panels stand, its balusters at 0.08 m so the guard reads as the print's dense iron band rather than a sparse row; and the light over the door made a door onto the deck (`hood.door_over`): in the print the window over the porch runs down behind the guard, its foot hidden, where the 0.6 m railing had stood under the window's sill at 7.5 m. Its leaves are the kit's French window (window_kit) from the second floor at 6.8 m, 0.05 m over the deck, to the storey's own head at 10.5 m, under the storey's crested cornice hood; the leaves themselves are behind the guard and out of the print, so their glazing is the kit's (L-k01-1816-henderson-1886).

boundary.note: The photograph's cast-iron fence on a stone curb along the street line, its gate at the stoop's foot and a side gate onto the south yard, as K11's scroll-band fence (T-2964: the photograph's panels are cast-iron scrollwork the full height of the fence; the kit's band of scrolls under its top rail is the nearest K11 has, the pattern the kit's). Its line is 7.4 m from the front, its curb just inside the 1904 parcel's street line (7.66 m); the lot's sides are the parcel's (data/street_grid/1904.json prairie_1816). T-3206: the entrance pair is drawn standing open into the yard, 70 degrees, so the walk's way in reads open from the street (reconstructed: no picture shows the leaves' state; liberty L-k14-walks-1800-block-3206).

bays.note: Two canted bays, each on the 1911 sheet's plan (s28fp-1816-b1 p2) and in the photograph: the street front's at its south corner, 6.87 m at the wall and 1.65 m out with 2.4 m of front, and the south flank's near its rear, 4.85 m at the wall and 1.0 m out with 2.68 m of front, each two storeys over the basement with a window in each face. T-2964: in the photograph both are carried up past the cornice, the bracketed cornice run round each, into a mansard of their own: the front's a raised crown whose deck stands over the main curb, the flank's lower; each under its own iron cresting. K08's mansard bay roof (roof.mansard) builds them: 4.4 m of lower face on the front's and 4.0 m on the flank's at 76 degrees, then a deck at a tenth. The rises are read through the photograph's camera as fractions of the wall under them (the front's crown about a third of the corner's height from grade to cornice, the flank's about two-fifths), so the crown's deck stands 0.4 m over the main curb, and are good to about half a metre; the pitch is the main mansard's near enough. The dormers in the bays' own faces are not built (the match record). T-1886: both bays stand on the house's stone basement, as the photograph shows them (the pale ashlar run round their faces to the water table at 2.0 m, a barred light under each window it sees): laid in the front's stone with brick over a 2.0 m basement storey (fabric front_stone, brick_above_m 2.0, T-2914), their principal-storey sash unmoved (sills 0.6 m over the floor). Both crowns' lower faces in the main mansard's slate (roof.slated_as_house), as the print draws all three alike, and one pedimented dormer on each crown's front face (mansard_dormers): the front crown's on its street face, the flank crown's on its south face, where the print shows them (x 600-690 and 175-240 px). T-1886 (2026-11-12): every light of both bays' two storeys over the basement carries K09's carved crest on its lintel (crest, the front hoods' own: 1.0 m wide or the lintel's top, 0.35 m high, 0.1 m proud), as the photograph draws the bays' hoods crested as the front's are (x 140-215 and 490-560 px); the carving is the kit's, the print resolving only a raised scrolled block. The flank crown's second dormer, in its south-east canted face, is not built: K08 lays a bay's dormers on its front face only (open on the match record; L-k01-1816-henderson-1886). T-1886 (2026-11-13): the flank bay re-read with the photograph through its corrected camera, the sheet's 4.85 m at the wall and 1.0 m out kept. The print draws the bay's south-east cant 91 px wide (x 233-324) and its south face 34 px (x 199-233), where the sheet's 1.085 m cant and 2.68 m front drew them about equal (76 and 75 px): the print's widths want a cant about 1.8 m along the wall and a front about 1.25 m (91 and 34 px within 1 px), a cant as shallow as the front bay's own; no 45-degree cant fits them. The crown's pedimented dormer stands on that narrow front in the print, and K08 lays a crown dormer clear of the hips by 0.3 m at the curb, so the plan is the narrowest front that keeps it (its sash 0.5 m): a cant 1.65 m along the wall and a 1.55 m front, drawn about 89 and 44 px, the front about 0.3 m wider than the print's (the match record). The wide light the print shows is the cant's, so the cant carries the wide light, 0.8 m (the print's about 1.0 m; at 1.0 m its recess runs behind the house wall on so shallow a cant), and the front a 0.75 m one, and both storeys' lights stand lower and shorter than the front bay's, as the print draws them (the windows' why_not_ordinary). The crown's lower face rises 3.25 m, not 4.0: through the corrected camera its curb's top stands at y 205 px in the print, about 40 px under the 4.0 m crown's, about 0.75 m at the crown. The whole bay draws about 28 px east of the print's along the flank, the plan and the camera's fit disagreeing there (the match record), so the reading is of its faces' widths and heights, not its place. Both crowns' dormers stand as the main mansard's now do (face 0.05 m in from the fascia, sash on a 0.1 m sill): the print draws the flank crown's sitting on the crown's cornice (its foot at y 400 px), where the build's stood about 0.6 m over it.

mansard.note: A slated mansard over the cornice, its lower faces steep and slightly swelling, with dormers in them: two on the street face, over the door and over the north windows, and one on the south face, where the photograph shows them (set 9.0, 12.5 and 7.4 m along their faces). T-2964: the photograph's dormers are square-headed under pediments, built as K01's gabled dormer head (head: gable, 40 degrees; their carved cheeks are not modelled), and iron cresting runs along the curb of every deck it shows, as 1801's deck carries it (mansard.deck.cresting, K10's iron ridge cresting, its pattern the kit's): along the main deck's street curb, and round the two bays' crowns (bays). The main deck's south curb, behind the flank bay's crown, shows none in the print, and its north and rear curbs are out of the camera's sight, so none of the three carries it: about 840 triangles a metre of iron are spent only where a picture shows them. T-1886 (2026-11-13): through the corrected camera the print stands every main dormer's sill on the cornice (the south one's at y 370 px, the cornice's top there 365-375), where the build's stood about 1 m over it (its sill at 280, the cornice 335): the three dormers' faces are brought out to 0.05 m in from the fascia's face and their sashes onto a 0.1 m sill, the kit's least, which lowers them about half a metre. The south dormer stands at u 6.6, not 7.4: the print draws it at x 335-385 px, close east of the flank crown, and the build's at 385-415; read against the south-east corner (the camera's anchor) it is 1.0 m west, against the flank bay (which itself draws 28 px east of the print's) 0.4 m, so 0.8 m splits them, each within about 10 px.

rear_wings.note: The 1911 sheet's rear range behind the main body (s28fp-1816-b1 p2, 'rear2B': u 22.4 to 34.3 m and v 0.3 to 7.9 m in the lot's frame), two storeys under a flat tin deck; no picture shows it, so its storeys, windows and roof are reconstructed. The sheet's small step between it and the south flank (about 2.1 by 3.2 m) is left to T-2964.

grade_m.note: the app's ground over the house's lowest foot, measured in the published 1904 app (T-3206): the yard is lifted onto it so the lawn and the walk are not under it

yard.note: T-3206 (the owner, 2026-10-27: walks, gates and boundaries to the pictures). The walk in flags from the stoop's foot through the entrance gate to the public walk, the gate's width; the cinder service walk from the side gate back along the south lot line to the house's rear corner, the gate's width (the south yard is 6.6 m wide and the rest of it is left to the ground). RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's flags, their width and wear, the lawn and its bare strip are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; liberty L-k14-walks-1800-block-3206. T-3233: the lawn is the app's own ground (`lawn: none`), not the kit's turf sheet, which met the ground beside it in a straight line of another green; the yard's grass now runs on to the side yards' and the margin's with no seam.

stone_front.note: T-1886: the photograph's basement is smooth pale ashlar in level courses about a third of a metre high (joints about 17-18 px apart at the camera's 53.6 px/m), from grade to a projecting water table about 0.28 m deep (y 885-900 px at the south-east corner) at the principal floor, 2.0 m over grade; the brick stands on it. Built as K02's smooth limestone stopped at the principal floor (brick_above_m 2.0): three base courses of about 0.41 m up to the basement lights' heads under a 0.28 m coping (K01 lays the rusticated base to the lights' heads, so three courses, which only the Bedford profile allows at that height), and no stone belt across the brick (belts: []), which the print does not show at the second floor. The print is monochrome and does not name the stone; the limestone is reconstructed (L-k01-1816-henderson-1886).

side_base.note: T-1886: the photograph shows the south flank's basement, between its canted bay and the front's, in the same pale ashlar as the front's, up to the water table run round from the corner (y 885-900 px at x 588), with the brick only over it.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3S.B.; rear2B brick dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

what_it_supplies: the canted bay at the street front's south corner and the canted bay on the south flank, against the 1911 sheet's plan
the porch: turned columns on the stoop's landing, an entablature over them and an iron balcony on it
the storeys: a rusticated stone basement, two tall brick storeys, a bracketed cornice and a slated mansard with dormers
the windows: tall sash on the principal floor and shorter above, under carved hoods
what_it_does_not_supply: the north wall, the rear and the rear range

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2329) in place by T-2963 (piece 1 of T-1886), under the draft's own id, as a K01 brick frontage read off the one photograph of the house (chicagology_1816_henderson_photo, undated, after 1873) against the 1911 sheet's plan: the front block with its canted front bay and the porch beside it, the canted bay on the south flank, the rear range, and the mansard. The photograph's camera and match record are in data/reference_views/henderson_house_1816_prairie/; what it shows that is not built yet is open there for T-2964, with the 1874 Land Owner engraving.
